item.title: Companies Act: Joint Committee reports on the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026
item.description:
Companies Act · Committee report · JPC Report No. 1

Who it covers: Readers tracking the Bill. Proposal only; not in force.

  • Recommends limiting the 120-day charge registration window to prescribed classes of small companies.
  • Accepts the LLP extension of s. 185(1)(b).
  • Accepts the civil penalty for s. 186(9) and (10) register defaults without change.

Official source

item.title: Companies Act: DPT-3 for FY 2025-26 can be filed until 31-07-2026 without additional fee
item.description:
Companies Act · Circular · General Circular 2/2026

Effective 2026-06-19.

Who it covers: Companies filing the annual DPT-3 return, including particulars of loans received that are not deposits.

  • Additional fees are waived for DPT-3 for the year ended 31-03-2026 filed up to 31-07-2026.

Official source

item.title: Companies Act: Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 introduced: changes to charges, s. 185, s. 186 and compounding proposed
item.description:
Companies Act · Bill · Bill No. 85 of 2026

Who it covers: All companies, if enacted. Proposal only; not in force.

  • A 120-day further window to register charges is proposed for prescribed classes of companies.
  • s. 185(1)(b) would also cover LLPs in which a director or relative is a partner.
  • Defaults in keeping the s. 186 register would attract a civil penalty instead of a fine.
  • The Regional Director could compound offences with a maximum fine up to Rs 1 crore.
  • Small company ceilings in the Act would rise to Rs 20 crore and Rs 200 crore.

Official source

item.title: Companies Act: Registrars appointed afresh as adjudicating officers under s. 454
item.description:
Companies Act · Notification · S.O. 698(E)

Effective 2026-02-11.

Who it covers: Companies and officers facing penalties for defaults such as late charge or resolution filings.

  • Registrars of Companies are appointed as adjudicating officers with the jurisdictions listed in the notification.
  • The 2015 and 2019 appointment notifications are superseded.

Official source

item.title: Companies Act: Small company limits raised to Rs 10 crore paid-up capital and Rs 100 crore turnover
item.description:
Companies Act · Rules · G.S.R. 880(E)

Effective 2025-12-01.

Who it covers: Private companies that are not holding or subsidiary companies.

  • Rule 2(1)(t) is substituted: a small company's paid-up capital must not exceed Rs 10 crore and turnover must not exceed Rs 100 crore.

Official source

item.title: Companies Act: NBFC and IFSC finance company lending treated as 'financing industrial enterprises' for s. 186
item.description:
Companies Act · Rules · G.S.R. 811(E)

Effective 2025-11-03.

Who it covers: RBI-registered NBFCs and IFSCA-registered finance companies giving loans, guarantees or security in the ordinary course of business.

  • Rule 11(2) of the Board meetings rules is substituted.
  • An RBI-registered NBFC's loans, guarantees and security in the ordinary course of business count as 'business of financing industrial enterprises', so s. 186 (other than s. 186(1)) does not apply to them.
  • The same treatment now covers IFSCA-registered finance companies for their lending activities.

Official source
